annotation.title_clean: Autonomous delivery robots: a legal framework for infliction of game-theoretic small penalties on pedestrians
annotation.title_en: Autonomous delivery robots: a legal framework for infliction of game-theoretic small penalties on pedestrians
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Basu, S.; Omotubora, A.; Fox, C.
annotation.summary_en: Legal analysis of autonomous delivery robots that, per game theory, must make credible threats of small harm to negotiate space with pedestrians. It argues ADRs could be treated as pedestrians under existing law, proposes robot self-defence and property rights as justification, and examines collision liability and privacy/data protection.
key_provisions_or_claims: ADRs could be considered pedestrians under existing law.
Robot self-defence and defence of property proposed as legal basis for small penalties.
Game theory requires a non-zero collision probability as credible threat to avoid the freezing robot problem.
Liability analysed for deliberate and accidental collisions.
Privacy and data protection challenges arise from data used to model and predict interactions.
